sb_prompt: WHAT HOBBIES DO YOU HAVE IN YOUR SPARE TIME?  DO THEY INCLUDE ANY HANDICRAFTSWOODWORKING?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hi there.
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Did you get my message about the call?
ParticipantB: Yeah, I saw it. Hi.
ParticipantA: So, what do you like to do in your spare time?
ParticipantB: Oh, well, honestly? Not much right now. Work is pretty consuming. I'm a pharmacist, so it's mostly just being on my feet, dealing with prescriptions, you know?
ParticipantA: Oh, that sounds intense. I'm a librarian, so it's a lot quieter, but definitely busy too.
ParticipantB: Yeah, but different kind of busy. Mine is high-stakes sometimes. Like, if someone walks in there with a severe reaction, you gotta act fast.
ParticipantA: Right, that's good stuff. I mean, I don't have that kind of pressure. It's just... books. And quiet places.
ParticipantB: Books? Like, reading? Or do you do anything with them?
ParticipantA: Oh, actually, I do a little bit. I like woodworking. I've been making small stuff. Birdhouses, little shelves. Just nothing big.
ParticipantB: Woodworking? Oh, nice. I've thought about trying that. I mean, the idea of making something with your hands sounds nice.
ParticipantA: Yeah, it does. I guess I just started a few years ago. I didn't really have a reason, I just felt like it.
ParticipantB: Huh. Just felt like it? That's kind of hard to explain. I usually need a reason or a goal.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I know what you mean. It was just this quiet urge I've had since college. Never quite figured out why, but it stuck.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that's weird. I'm kind of the opposite. I like the idea of fixing things, but the actual process? It's not for me.
ParticipantA: Really? Why's that?
ParticipantB: Well, I have a cousin who got into woodworking, serious into it. He'd spend hours in the garage. And he got really stressed. Like, obsessed.
ParticipantA: Oh, wow. That's different. I thought everyone liked it because it was relaxing.
ParticipantB: For me, seeing that with him... it just made me realize I might not be the patient type. I get anxious if I can't just solve the problem immediately.
ParticipantA: Hmm. I guess I'm lucky. I just enjoy the process, even if I don't know why. It helps me unwind.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I get that. I just prefer fixing appliances or something quick. A little repair here, a little patch there.
ParticipantA: Oh, that makes sense. I'm glad you didn't end up making birdhouses, though. Maybe you'd hate it.
ParticipantB: Maybe. I'd probably break the saw. I don't know. But at least I'm not gonna ruin the whole project like my cousin did.
ParticipantA: True. I'm proud of my shelves, actually. Took me six months to get the legs right.
ParticipantB: Six months? Wow. I couldn't do that. I'd quit after an hour.
ParticipantA: I guess we're different. I'm patient; you're practical.
ParticipantB: Exactly. I mean, I appreciate the craft, I just don't have the temperament for the long haul.
ParticipantA: Fair enough. Well, I'm glad we talked about it. I think I might stick to birdhouses.
ParticipantB: Birdhouses sound nice. Quiet and simple. Maybe I'll just keep fixing my coffee maker instead.
ParticipantA: That works for me too. Thanks for chatting.
ParticipantB: Yeah, sure. You too.
